claim: The Reproducibility Project: Cancer Biology seeks to address growing concerns about reproducibility in scientific research by conducting replications of selected experiments from a number of high-profile papers in the field of cancer biology.
source: The Reproducibility Project: Cancer Biology seeks to address growing concerns about reproducibility in scientific research by conducting replications of selected experiments from a number of high-profile papers in the field of cancer biology.
evidence: This is a statement about the project's purpose and methodology, representing established knowledge about the project itself.

claim: The papers selected for replication were published between 2010 and 2012.
source: The papers, which were published between 2010 and 2012, were selected on the basis of citations and Altmetric scores (Errington et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to Errington et al., 2014, which describes the selection criteria.

claim: The papers for replication were selected on the basis of citations and Altmetric scores.
source: The papers, which were published between 2010 and 2012, were selected on the basis of citations and Altmetric scores (Errington et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Errington et al., 2014.

claim: Lu and colleagues published a paper titled 'IDH mutation impairs histone demethylation and results in a block to cell differentiation' in Nature in 2012.
source: This Registered Report describes the proposed replication plan of key experiments from "IDH mutation impairs histone demethylation and results in a block to cell differentiation" by Lu and colleagues, published in Nature in 2012 (Lu et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Lu et al., 2012.

claim: Lu and colleagues demonstrated that expression of mutant forms of IDH1 or IDH2 caused global increases in histone methylation.
source: Lu and colleagues demonstrated that expression of mutant forms of IDH1 or IDH2 caused global increases in histone methylation and increased levels of 2 hydroxyglutarate (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is supported by reference to Figure 1B from Lu et al., 2012.

claim: Expression of mutant forms of IDH1 or IDH2 increased levels of 2-hydroxyglutarate.
source: Lu and colleagues demonstrated that expression of mutant forms of IDH1 or IDH2 caused global increases in histone methylation and increased levels of 2 hydroxyglutarate (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is supported by reference to Figure 1B from Lu et al., 2012.

claim: Increased histone methylation from mutant IDH1/IDH2 expression was correlated with a block in differentiation.
source: This was correlated with a block in differentiation (Figures 2A, B and D).
evidence: This is supported by reference to Figures 2A, B and D from Lu et al., 2012.

claim: The differentiation block effect appeared to be mediated by the histone demethylase KDM4C.
source: This effect appeared to be mediated by the histone demethylase KDM4C (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is supported by reference to Figure 4D from Lu et al., 2012.

claim: Mutations in IDH1 and IDH2 are associated with gliomas.
source: Mutations in the metabolic proteins IDH1 and IDH2 are associated with gliomas, acute myeloid leukemias, chondrosarcomas, intrahepatic cholangiocarcinomas, lymphomas, melanomas and colon, thyroid and prostate cancers (for review, see Krell et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a review by Krell et al., 2013.

claim: IDH mutations change the specificity of the reaction catalyzed by IDH proteins such that they produce 2-hydroxyglutarate from isocitrate instead of α-ketoglutarate.
source: Previous work has shown that these mutations change the specificity of the reaction catalyzed by IDH proteins; instead of producing α-ketoglutarate from isocitrate, they produce 2-hydroxyglutarate (2HG), a metabolite that can have oncogenic effects (Krell et al., 2013; McKenney and Levine, 2013; Ward et al., 2010; Xu et al., 2011; Zhang et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations: Krell et al., 2013; McKenney and Levine, 2013; Ward et al., 2010; Xu et al., 2011; Zhang et al., 2013.

claim: 2-hydroxyglutarate is a metabolite that can have oncogenic effects.
source: Previous work has shown that these mutations change the specificity of the reaction catalyzed by IDH proteins; instead of producing α-ketoglutarate from isocitrate, they produce 2-hydroxyglutarate (2HG), a metabolite that can have oncogenic effects (Krell et al., 2013; McKenney and Levine, 2013; Ward et al., 2010; Xu et al., 2011; Zhang et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations: Krell et al., 2013; McKenney and Levine, 2013; Ward et al., 2010; Xu et al., 2011; Zhang et al., 2013.

claim: 2HG interferes with global demethylation that is required for progenitor cells to complete terminal differentiation.
source: They present evidence that 2HG interferes with global demethylation that is required for progenitor cells to complete terminal differentiation.
evidence: This is a summary of evidence presented by Lu et al., 2012, as described in the manuscript.

claim: Transfection of 3T3-L1 cells with mutant forms of IDH1 and IDH2 that produce 2HG led to an increase in global methylation levels.
source: Transfection of 3T3-L1 cells with the mutant forms of IDH1 and IDH2 that produce 2HG lead to an increase in global methylation levels and prevented normal in vitro differentiation into adipocytes.
evidence: This is a summary of findings from Lu et al., 2012.

claim: Transfection of 3T3-L1 cells with mutant forms of IDH1 and IDH2 that produce 2HG prevented normal in vitro differentiation into adipocytes.
source: Transfection of 3T3-L1 cells with the mutant forms of IDH1 and IDH2 that produce 2HG lead to an increase in global methylation levels and prevented normal in vitro differentiation into adipocytes.
evidence: This is a summary of findings from Lu et al., 2012.

claim: The histone demethylase KDM4C is sensitive to 2HG.
source: The 2HG-sensitive histone demethylase KDM4C appeared to be required for this process, as knockdown of KDM4C recapitulated the phenotype of 2HG production.
evidence: This is a summary of findings from Lu et al., 2012.

claim: Knockdown of KDM4C recapitulated the phenotype of 2HG production.
source: The 2HG-sensitive histone demethylase KDM4C appeared to be required for this process, as knockdown of KDM4C recapitulated the phenotype of 2HG production.
evidence: This is a summary of findings from Lu et al., 2012.

claim: There is a correlation between IDH mutation status and level of overall methylation in glioma samples.
source: Examination of glioma samples showed a correlation between IDH mutation status and level of overall methylation (Lu et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Lu et al., 2012.

claim: Lu and colleagues transfected mutant and wild type forms of IDH1 and IDH2 into 293T cells and used Western blot to assess the levels of various methylation markers.
source: In Figure 1B, Lu and colleagues examined the effects of mutations in IDH1 and IDH2 on global levels of methylation by transfecting mutant and wild type forms of the genes into 293T cells and using Western blot to assess the levels of various methylation markers.
evidence: This describes the methodology from Lu et al., 2012, Figure 1B.

claim: Lu and colleagues confirmed that introduction of mutated forms of IDH1 and IDH2 correlated with increased intracellular levels of 2HG.
source: They also confirmed that introduction of the mutated forms of IDH1 and IDH2 correlated with increased intracellular levels of the oncometabolite 2HG.
evidence: This is a summary of findings from Lu et al., 2012.

claim: Mutations in IDH1 and IDH2 correlate with increased levels of many methylation markers.
source: Their findings suggest that mutations in IDH1 and IDH2 correlate with increased levels of many methylation markers, and this key finding is replicated in Protocol 1.
evidence: This is a summary of findings from Lu et al., 2012.

claim: When treated with appropriate signals, 3T3-L1 cells undergo epigenetic changes required for them to differentiate into adipocytes.
source: In order to understand the effects of hypermethylation more fully, Lu and colleagues turned to an in vitro model of differentiation; when treated with appropriate signals, 3T3-L1 cells undergo epigenetic changes required for them to differentiation into adipocytes.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the 3T3-L1 cell differentiation model.

claim: Differentiated 3T3-L1 cells transfected with vector only or wild type IDH2 showed robust Oil-Red-O staining.
source: While differentiated 3T3-L1 cells transfected with vector only or wild type IDH2 showed robust Oil-Red-O staining, cells transfected with mutant IDH2 did not, indicating a block in differentiation.
evidence: This is a summary of findings from Lu et al., 2012, Figures 2A and B.

claim: 3T3-L1 cells transfected with mutant IDH2 did not show robust Oil-Red-O staining, indicating a block in differentiation.
source: While differentiated 3T3-L1 cells transfected with vector only or wild type IDH2 showed robust Oil-Red-O staining, cells transfected with mutant IDH2 did not, indicating a block in differentiation.
evidence: This is a summary of findings from Lu et al., 2012, Figures 2A and B.

claim: Cells transfected with mutant IDH variants did not express high levels of known adipocyte markers as confirmed by qRT-PCR.
source: qRT-PCR confirmed that cells transfected with mutant IDH variants did not express high levels of known adipocyte markers (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is a summary of findings from Lu et al., 2012, Figure 2D.

claim: KDM4C is expressed as 3T3-L1 differentiation progresses.
source: Lu and colleagues identified a histone demethylase, KDM4C, expressed as 3T3-L1 differentiation progressed, that appeared to be sensitive to 2HG.
evidence: This is a summary of findings from Lu et al., 2012.

claim: Loss of KDM4C increased global methylation levels.
source: Western blot analysis and Oil-Red-O staining confirmed that loss of KDM4C increased global methylation levels and inhibited differentiation.
evidence: This is a summary of findings from Lu et al., 2012, Figure 4D.

claim: Loss of KDM4C inhibited differentiation.
source: Western blot analysis and Oil-Red-O staining confirmed that loss of KDM4C increased global methylation levels and inhibited differentiation.
evidence: This is a summary of findings from Lu et al., 2012, Figure 4D.

claim: Overexpression of the IDH1R132H allele in human tumor cell lines increased global histone methylation levels.
source: Multiple groups have demonstrated that perturbations in IDH proteins alter methylation levels; overexpression of the IDH1R132H allele in human tumor cells lines increased global histone methylation levels (Duncan et al., 2012), exogenous IDH2R140Q increased methylation levels in erythroleukemia progenitor cells (Kernytsky et al., 2015) and an immortalized astrocyte cell line expressing IDH1R132H also demonstrated increased levels of methylation (Turcan et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Duncan et al., 2012.

claim: Exogenous IDH2R140Q increased methylation levels in erythroleukemia progenitor cells.
source: Multiple groups have demonstrated that perturbations in IDH proteins alter methylation levels; overexpression of the IDH1R132H allele in human tumor cells lines increased global histone methylation levels (Duncan et al., 2012), exogenous IDH2R140Q increased methylation levels in erythroleukemia progenitor cells (Kernytsky et al., 2015) and an immortalized astrocyte cell line expressing IDH1R132H also demonstrated increased levels of methylation (Turcan et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Kernytsky et al., 2015.

claim: An immortalized astrocyte cell line expressing IDH1R132H demonstrated increased levels of methylation.
source: Multiple groups have demonstrated that perturbations in IDH proteins alter methylation levels; overexpression of the IDH1R132H allele in human tumor cells lines increased global histone methylation levels (Duncan et al., 2012), exogenous IDH2R140Q increased methylation levels in erythroleukemia progenitor cells (Kernytsky et al., 2015) and an immortalized astrocyte cell line expressing IDH1R132H also demonstrated increased levels of methylation (Turcan et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Turcan et al., 2012.

claim: Members of the Thompson lab confirmed that expression of mutant variants of IDH proteins in 3T3-L1 cells blocked differentiation into adipocytes.
source: Members of the Thompson lab (authors of this study) have confirmed that expression of mutant variants of IDH proteins in 3T3-L1 cells blocked differentiation into adipocytes (Londono Gentile et al., 2013; Ward et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Londono Gentile et al., 2013 and Ward et al., 2013.

claim: Mutant IDH1 expression increased levels of methylation in mice.
source: Sasaki and colleagues have shown that mutant IDH1 expression increased levels of methylation in mice (Sasaki et al., 2012), while Akbay and colleagues published a similar observation for mutant forms of IDH2 (Akbay et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Sasaki et al., 2012.

claim: Mutant forms of IDH2 increased levels of methylation in mice.
source: Sasaki and colleagues have shown that mutant IDH1 expression increased levels of methylation in mice (Sasaki et al., 2012), while Akbay and colleagues published a similar observation for mutant forms of IDH2 (Akbay et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Akbay et al., 2014.

claim: There is a marked increase in H3K9me3 levels associated with IDH mutations in oligodendromas.
source: This effect may even hold true for human patients, as there is a marked increase in H3K9me3 levels associated with IDH mutations in oligodendromas and high grade astrocytomas (Venneti et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Venneti et al., 2013.

claim: There is a marked increase in H3K9me3 levels associated with IDH mutations in high grade astrocytomas.
source: This effect may even hold true for human patients, as there is a marked increase in H3K9me3 levels associated with IDH mutations in oligodendromas and high grade astrocytomas (Venneti et al., 2013).
